chapter: Touring, band and money in the 1950s-60s
title: Police beating in Monroe in 1963
summary: In 1963 on the way to a job he was hit on the head by police, was paralyzed and hospitalized; he lists his band members then.

bands.name: Sugar Boy and His Cane Cutters

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Got hurt. Got my head bust. In 1963, police hit me. Yeah, what happened?
I heard about that. Somebody told him.

I was in Monroe. Wow. He stopped me from speeding and he said I was drunk and I wasn't doing either one. I wasn't drunk and I wasn't speeding and I hit him in my head and I was paralyzed and I was in the hospital and I had to be operated on. I stayed in the hospital. I stayed in the hospital three weeks from that and I was on the I list for about a week, I guess. I had a slim chance of making it. I did. I made it. So this is what happened. Well, this happened in 1963. You were coming from a job. You just went on a job. I was going on a job. With Smiley Lewis and well, just myself. Who was in your band? At that time?
I was going on a job. Smiley Lewis and myself. The band and Smiley Lewis.

You must have had a different band by then. Oh yeah. Let me see. The only person that was, I think Big Bob Miles was the only person that was playing in the band with me. That was with me when I started. I think. I don't know. No Big Bob Miles wasn't in the band either. Now Batman played with me.
Ranking. D-Roy Ranking. I see Batman, Buddy Williams played drums. Frank Field was playing bass. Smiley Lewis was playing guitar.
